title: Choose the visual world for Stringline
question: The roll assigned The Overnight Book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Overnight Book
options.lineage: The crew's carbon-copy appointment book and estimate pad
options.thesis: The page is your appointment book, and it fills itself while you sleep.
options.viewport: One giant appointment-book page for Thursday: red pre-printed time rows, blue entries landing one by one overnight, the headline in the page's header line, and a stamped Join the pilot list box at its foot.
options.risk: Turns into paper-craft costume if the handwriting or paper texture is faked cheaply.

raised.raise: Every entry carries its own cross-check: answered in 38 s, booked 4 min later, so the book proves speed, not just volume.
One text size for every entry; rank comes from weight and ink colour, never from a pile of sizes. Less information per screen.
Total palette commitment: only the form's own inks (canary, pink copy, red rule, blue ballpoint), nothing else on the page.

options.label: The Idea Book
options.lineage: Paver manufacturers' glossy idea books that contractors hand to homeowners
options.thesis: The page is an idea book where every spread is a homeowner's own yard, rendered and priced.
options.viewport: A full-bleed patio concept render with the homeowner's before photo inset, the headline set like a catalog cover line, and the action beside a swatch strip.
options.risk: The most familiar of the set, close to what paver brands already ship, and it needs generated photography to work.

options.label: Night Instrument Six-Pack
options.lineage: a small plane's six night gauges
options.thesis: Six gauges a contractor cross-checks: leads, response time, qualified, booked, shown, cost.
options.viewport: Two rows of three glowing dials over black, with the action as a placard.
options.case: Fuses as a results dashboard, but contractors don't see themselves in a cockpit, and booking reads weaker than in the book.
options.kept: Each booked entry shows its timing cross-check.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: Consults listed like departures on a raked timetable.
options.viewport: Raked slides of consult times sliding across a lit goldenrod bed.
options.case: Schedules fuse well, but the raked glass is foreign to the trade and buries the offer.
options.kept: One type size; rank by weight and case.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Every lead as a bar in a strobing barcode field.
options.viewport: A wall of barcode bars that inverts once.
options.case: Loses on both axes: abstract data art says nothing to a hardscaper.
options.risk: Cold and unreadable for this audience.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: One red ribbon follows a lead from call to shown consult.
options.viewport: A single ribbon running down a buff sheet through dated folds.
options.case: The chain fuses neatly, but it reads museum, not jobsite.
options.kept: Known versus pending states on every entry.

options.label: Penny-Press Broadside
options.thesis: The overnight lead told as a shouting news sheet.
options.viewport: A wood-type headline over an engraving band and two dense columns.
options.case: Dense columns are the 'too much information' problem again.

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.lineage: an installation sun in a hazed hall
options.thesis: A vast amber hall with the offer on its horizon.
options.viewport: A half sun on the far wall, silhouettes on the floor.
options.case: Atmospheric but says nothing about leads or consults.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A field-service software site like Jobber or Housecall Pro, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and email field on the left, a product screenshot on the right, logos below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
